summary: A long, sometimes curved mussel, up to nine inches, that shelters under slabs of rock in big rivers.
description: A large, greatly lengthened shell, sometimes curved, reaching at least 9 inches.  Young shells are light yellow, greenish-tan, or brown.  Old ones are rough and dark brown to black.  The inside is white.
habitat: Large rivers, in riffles and shoals, often sheltered under slabs of rock or ledges.
alabama: The Muscle Shoals reach of the Tennessee River once held a large population, and dams took most of its habitat.  The listing rule knew of about ten live mussels found at three sites below Guntersville Dam between 1997 and 1999, and called the status of the Tennessee River population unknown.
countiesText: Along the Tennessee River
range: Large rivers of the Mississippi and Ohio basins
threats: Dams and reservoirs, which flooded its habitat and split what was left, and the cold water let out below them.  Zebra mussels are a further threat, and few young are being raised.

range: Rivers of the Ohio, Tennessee, upper Mississippi, and Great Lakes basins
threats: Dams and reservoirs, which break up its habitat, along with pollution, spills, and zebra mussels.
